title: Repeat Cracking in the Aft Cargo Compartment Sill Area — Request for a Permanent Design Solution
abstract: Operator request for a permanent structural answer to repeated cracking found along the aft cargo compartment sill on the highest-cycle aircraft of a short-sector CIRRANE-13 fleet, after four temporary repairs in two years.

sections.request: We keep finding cracks in the same place along the bottom edge of the rear hold on our oldest CIRRANE-13 aircraft. It is always the left side, always in the corner where the hold floor meets the fuselage, and it always turns up during the C-check rather than in service. Four of our aircraft have been through this area now and two of them twice. The second time on one aircraft the crack was longer than our approved repair allows, so we had to keep the aircraft on the ground for five days while we waited for an engineering answer. Our line stations have started treating the area as a known problem and look at it whenever the hold is empty, which is not a way to run a fleet. What we want is a design change that stops the cracking, not another repair on top of a repair, and we want to be able to do it during a normal C-check without stripping the whole hold lining out.
sections.background: The first finding was reported to us by our maintenance provider in early 2024 on an aircraft that had passed 21 000 flight cycles. We fly short sectors, six to eight a day, so our aircraft reach cycle counts much faster than the fleet average and we tend to see cycle-driven findings before anyone else. Since then we have carried out four temporary repairs on three aircraft. All of them are in the same lower corner region on the left-hand side, between the rear hold door sill and the bulk hold divider. Our reliability team records 3.4 unscheduled structural events per 1000 flight cycles on that zone against a fleet baseline of 0.6. We have already embodied the corrosion protection improvement in the rear lower shell that was recommended to us, and the cracking carried on afterwards, so we do not think this is a corrosion problem.
sections.expected_outcome: A design change that removes the repeat inspection of the rear hold sill area, applicable to the aircraft we already operate, with a retrofit that fits inside a scheduled C-check and does not need a dedicated aircraft-on-ground event or a full removal of the hold lining.

type_data.business_justification: Unscheduled downtime on the aft cargo sill has cost the operator an estimated 31 aircraft-days over two years across a nineteen-aircraft sub-fleet, and the repeat inspection consumes about 40 manhours per C-check on every aircraft in the group.
